unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 1 month (the common period occurring most frequently). Unit-periods per year (w) = 12. Per Appendix J (b)(5)(ii), the number of full unit-periods between two dates is the number of months measured back from the later date. From 1-10-78 to 2-10-78 = 1 full month with 0 remaining days. Therefore t = 1, f = 0.
computation: Special form for single-advance regular payments: A = (1/((1+fi)(1+i)^t)) * P * a_n_due(1+i). Substituting values: 5000 = (1/((1+0*i)(1+i)^1)) * 230 * ((1-(1+i)^(-24))/i)*(1+i). This simplifies to the ordinary-annuity form: 5000 = 230 * (1-(1+i)^(-24))/i. Solved for the unit-period rate i by iteration (e.g., Newton-Raphson or bisection carried to sufficient precision): i ≈ 0.0080714234. Annual percentage rate I = w*i = 12 * 0.0080714234 = 0.096857... Rounded to two decimals per Appendix J: 9.69%.
weakest_point: None; values, dates, and APR are verbatim from the official Appendix J example and the equation reproduces the stated rate to within rounding.

case_name: Irregular first period (long first period) — Appendix J (c)(1)(ii)
unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 1 month (most frequent common period). Unit-periods per year (w) = 12. Per Appendix J (b)(5)(ii), measure back from the later date (4-1-78): one full month is 3-1-78 to 4-1-78, so t = 1. The remaining fraction is measured forward from the earlier date to the beginning of the first full unit-period: 2-10-78 to 3-1-78 = 19 days. Fraction f = 19/30. The fractional-period rate is f*i per Appendix J (b)(6).
computation: Special form: A = (1/((1+fi)(1+i)^t)) * P * a_n_due(1+i). Substituting values: 6000 = (1/((1+(19/30)i)(1+i)^1)) * 200 * ((1-(1+i)^(-36))/i)*(1+i). Solved for i by iteration: i ≈ 0.0098470902. Annual percentage rate I = w*i = 12 * 0.0098470902 = 0.118165... Rounded to two decimals per Appendix J: 11.82%.
weakest_point: None; follows the official example exactly. The 19-day odd-period fraction (19/30) is the distinctive Appendix J unit-period rule that diverges from generic calendar-day APR math.

unit_period_analysis: Single-advance, single-payment transaction. Per Appendix J (b)(4)(ii), the unit-period shall be the term of the transaction, not exceeding 1 year. The term is 255 days (less than 1 year), so unit-period = 255 days. Per Appendix J (b)(5)(vii), for a term less than a year not equal to a whole number of months, unit-periods in the term = 1 and unit-periods per year (w) = 365/255. From 1-3-78 to 9-15-78 = 255 days, so t = 1, f = 0.
computation: Special form (Form 4): A = P/((1+fi)(1+i)^t). Substituting values: 1000 = 1080/((1+0*i)(1+i)^1). Direct algebraic solution: 1+i = 1080/1000 = 1.08, so i = 0.08. (Form 1 gives the same result directly: I = 100*w*(P/A - 1) = 100*(365/255)*(1080/1000 - 1) = 11.4510...%) Annual percentage rate I = w*i = (365/255)*0.08 = 0.114510... Rounded to two decimals per Appendix J: 11.45%.
weakest_point: None; the direct algebraic solution confirms the iteration result exactly. The unit-period rule (255-day unit-period, w = 365/255) is the Appendix J-specific feature.

unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 1 month. Unit-periods per year (w) = 12. Regular first period: from 1-10-78 to 2-10-78 = 1 full month, so t = 1, f = 0. The final payment is irregular in amount but occurs at the regular time (the 24th monthly interval from the first payment).
computation: Special form for odd final payment: A = (1/((1+fi)(1+i)^t)) * [P * a_{n-1}_due(1+i) + Pn/(1+i)^{n-1}]. Substituting values: 5000 = (1/((1+0*i)(1+i)^1)) * [230 * ((1-(1+i)^(-23))/i)*(1+i) + 280/(1+i)^23]. Solved for i by iteration: i ≈ 0.0087503907. Annual percentage rate I = w*i = 12 * 0.0087503907 = 0.105005... Rounded to two decimals per Appendix J: 10.50%.
weakest_point: None; follows the official example exactly. The equation structure (annuity due for first n-1 payments plus discounted final payment) is the Appendix J special form for this irregularity.

case_name: Complex single advance with irregular payment schedule — Appendix J (c)(6)(iii)

inputs.payment_schedule: 360 monthly payments, constant for 12 months at a time

unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 1 month (most frequent common period). Unit-periods per year (w) = 12. Per Appendix J (b)(5)(ii), measure back from 6-1-78: one full month is 5-1-78 to 6-1-78, so t = 1. Remaining fraction measured forward from 4-10-78 to 5-1-78 = 21 days, so f = 21/30. The 360 payments are irregular because the amount changes each year (12 payments at one amount, then 12 at the next, etc.).
weakest_point: The 360-term summation is rendered compactly via sigma notation with grouped annual amounts; every payment value is exact from the official example, but a mechanical recomputation must expand the summation to 360 individual terms.
